General.Description:
Deep in the Brazilian Amazon, beyond the last navigable stretch of the Rio Negro, exists a region known locally as the Zona Branca — the White Zone. Satellite imagery shows only unbroken forest canopy. Ground surveys have never penetrated more than forty kilometres. And yet, according to a dying anthropologist's encrypted field notes, somewhere in the Zona Branca is evidence of a pre-Columbian civilisation far older and far more sophisticated than anything previously theorised.

Archaeologist Dr. Sofia Alves has spent her career working within the Brazilian academic system, navigating bureaucracy and funding shortfalls with patience and tenacity. When the field notes arrive — encoded in a cipher using an extinct Amazonian dialect she happens to specialise in — she knows this is the discovery she has worked her whole life toward. She also knows that others want the notes, and that some of them are not interested in scientific discovery.

The Amazon Code is a rich, exhilarating adventure novel that layers archaeological mystery, political thriller, and ecological drama against the breathtaking backdrop of the world's largest rainforest. Renata Silveira writes the Amazon as few outsiders can — with intimacy, respect, and wonder.

A journey into the green unknown.
